chapter_title: 第158章 笑盈盈的應禪溪

segments.title: 第158章 笑盈盈的應禪溪
segments.content:
The Verdant Years Reignited, Chapter 158: The Beaming Ying Chanxi

Li Luo hadn't just said that casually.

Because in his past life, the first time he went to Yan Zhusheng's house for an interview, Yan Zhusheng had asked him to record a video and audio of her singing.

As long as the edited video met Yan Zhusheng's standards, the contract could be signed on the spot.

Back then, Li Luo was simply struck by Yan Zhusheng's beauty, thinking that such a gorgeous girl must have very high standards.

He was just a dilettante who had entered the online literature and short drama market halfway, and his video editing skills were at a beginner's level.

So, the simpler and more relaxed the interview seemed, the more Li Luo felt he wouldn't be chosen.

Thus, with the mindset of just listening and enjoying the beautiful sight, he helped Yan Zhusheng set up the camera and prepare the microphone and recording equipment.

But when Yan Zhusheng finished the main verse of the song "The Sky Has No Limits" and abruptly launched into the climactic chorus, Li Luo was instantly stunned.

Even after Yan Zhusheng had finished the entire song, he remained in a daze, unable to snap out of it for a long time.

That was the first time he had appreciated singing of such a caliber up close, in person.

It felt even better than the concerts he had accompanied Xu Youyu to.

From that moment on, Yan Zhusheng's rendition of "The Sky Has No Limits" was deeply imprinted in his mind.

Bringing out this song today was, in a way, a subconscious choice on his part.

However, compared to the thirty-something Yan Zhusheng, when the sixteen-year-old Yan Zhusheng sang this song, it was more the inherently bright and clear music that was captivating.

Whereas when the Yan Zhusheng of his past life sang this song, besides her high-pitched timbre, which was like a clear spring, there was also a flavor of personal insight and a faint sense of world-weariness.

It had a unique charm.

One could only say they each had their own merits. Yan Zhusheng was still young now, after all, so one couldn't ask for too much.

To sing a heart-wrenching song, she first had to confess to Li Luo and get rejected just to barely bring out that flavor. One couldn't expect her to have much more emotional detail in her songs.

Right now, Yan Zhusheng could dominate at school, partly because it was truly rare for a high school student to sing at her level.

On the other hand, it was also because her physical functions were at a relative peak in her life, and she had been trained and nurtured since childhood by Yuan Wanqing, a professional singer.

If she wanted to take another step forward in the emotional details of her songs, it was not something that could be achieved through simple practice.

On this Saturday, after the morning self-study session ended, Li Luo and Yan Zhusheng packed their school bags and went to the doorway of Class One on the fourth floor.

When Ying Chanxi saw the two of them, she jogged over to the door and said to Li Luo, "I have to go to the competition class this afternoon. I won't be home until early evening, so you should head back first."

"Okay," Li Luo nodded. "I just happened to write another song and plan to go to Yan Zhusheng's house to record it this afternoon. I'll be back in the early evening. You and senior remember to buy groceries."

Hearing this, Ying Chanxi subconsciously glanced at Yan Zhusheng, then her gaze fell on Li Luo's face, her own expression instantly becoming reserved. "Oh, is that so? Is Zhusheng coming over for dinner tonight? I'll buy some of her favorite dishes."

"She'll probably stay at her mom's for dinner," Li Luo said, turning his head to look at Yan Zhusheng.

Yan Zhusheng blinked, showing no intention of evading. Instead, she said seriously, "My mom is very busy. She probably won't have time to eat with me tonight."

"Then come over together," Ying Chanxi said with a beaming smile. "I remember Zhusheng likes to eat swamp eel, right? I'll go to the market with senior to buy some later."

"Oh, thank you, Xixi," Yan Zhusheng said, a little pleased, probably because Ying Chanxi remembered what she liked to eat.

"That's settled then, we're leaving," Li Luo said, about to turn and leave with Yan Zhusheng.

But Ying Chanxi called out to him, pulling his body back.

Then she walked up to Li Luo and stood before him, reaching out to unwind the red scarf from his neck, and then carefully put it back on for him. "How did you even put this on? It's all crooked, it looks terrible."

"You tied it too tight for me..." Li Luo's lips twitched. "Are you trying to strangle me?"

"Hehe," Ying Chanxi said with a grin. "How could I?"

As she spoke, she loosened the scarf for Li Luo. "Is this better?"

"Much better." Li Luo touched the soft scarf on his neck and then said, "I'm off then."

"Go on." Ying Chanxi waved. "Remember to sing the new song when you get back tonight. I want to hear it too."

"OK, no problem."

After watching Li Luo and Yan Zhusheng go downstairs, Ying Chanxi walked to the corridor railing and looked down.

A moment later, she saw Li Luo and Yan Zhusheng emerge from the first-floor stairwell.

As the two walked onto Houde Road, they were talking softly with each other, not looking particularly intimate.

But just as they were halfway, Yan Zhusheng suddenly took out a pair of Bluetooth earbuds from her pocket, picked one up, and stuck it directly into Li Luo's ear before putting the other one in her own.

Watching this scene, Ying Chanxi rested her small fists on the railing. They clenched inexplicably, her fingers rubbing against each other, as if something was missing from her hands.

Finally, she let out a slightly unhappy hum and returned to the classroom to get ready for her competition class.

"Class monitor, I'm planning to sneak out for a cup of milk tea before class," Xie Shuchen sidled up at this moment and whispered. "What flavor do you want?"

Ying Chanxi glanced at him and suddenly asked, "Doesn't your rock club have practice this afternoon?"

"We were supposed to," Xie Shuchen said, pausing for a moment. "But I have to attend the competition class. And it just so happens that Li Luo and Yan Zhusheng also have things to do this afternoon, so we moved it to tomorrow's evening self-study."

"Besides, we've practiced quite a bit these past few days. Li Luo wrote a new song, and we plan to make a stunning debut at the New Year's Day Gala!"

"Make sure you watch carefully then, class monitor. It's definitely going to be spectacular!"

After hearing Xie Shuchen's words, the thought of Li Luo and Yan Zhusheng standing on stage together, shining brilliantly, made Ying Chanxi's eyes narrow.

"Strictly speaking, if you're staying at school after classes end on a Saturday for competition classes or club activities, you're not allowed to leave campus temporarily," Ying Chanxi said with a serious face. "I suggest you'd best not do this kind of thing in front of the class monitor."

Xie Shuchen looked completely baffled. "...Wait, what?"

It's fine if you don't want any, but why are you stopping me from buying some?

Didn't you always turn a blind eye before?

On the other side.

After Yan Zhusheng put the earbud in his ear, Li Luo took out his phone, checked QQ, and saw a message from his editor.

Qian Zhou: I've arrived at the place you mentioned. The First Affiliated High School of Qianjiang University in Yuhang City, right?

Qian Zhou: This school seems pretty good, huh? Right next to Qianjiang University.

Qian Zhou: I just asked the owner of the clothing store on the roadside. This is a provincial key high school? Don't tell me you're actually good at studying?

To be fair, during his time as an editor at Wenyue Group, Qian Zhou had heard quite a few industry rumors from the veteran editors.

Among them, minors writing online novels wasn't a particularly rare occurrence.

It was just that it was rare for them to achieve success.

But for someone to be successful in online literature while also excelling academically in high school was truly unheard of.

However, if Li Luo knew what his editor was thinking, he definitely would have burst out laughing.

Even setting aside a cheat like himself, there was also a freak like Xu Youyu, whose situation was even more absurd than his.

Chong Ran: Yeah, I just got out of class. I'm almost at the school gate.

Qian Zhou: OKOK.

Qian Zhou: I'm wearing a black down jacket, on the street opposite the school gate.

Chong Ran: I have a red scarf around my neck and a pair of white sneakers. There's also an incredibly beautiful girl next to me. You'll definitely be able to recognize me at a glance.

Qian Zhou: ?

Although he sent a question mark, the moment Qian Zhou saw Li Luo and Yan Zhusheng walk out of the school gate, he instantly locked onto them.

Indeed, he could recognize them at a glance.

Damn it!

What kind of life winner is this kid?

Qian Zhou looked speechlessly as Chong Ran crossed the crosswalk and came to stand before him, momentarily at a loss for words.

This young lady next to him, could she be his girlfriend?

Having such a beautiful girlfriend at such a young age, studying at a provincial key high school so his grades couldn't be too bad, and now he's written an online novel that can earn over 40,000 yuan a month.

And who knows how much his income will increase after it goes on all channels.

At this thought, Qian Zhou, a miserable corporate drone, immediately felt a suffocating pressure wash over him, finding himself surprisingly intimidated by this detestable high school student.

As for Li Luo, after arriving in front of Qian Zhou, he also briefly sized up his editor.

In his memory, when he entered the online literature industry after graduating from college, the editor named Qian Zhou was already the chief editor of the urban genre.

This was the first time Li Luo had seen this future chief editor in person.

He was chubby and not tall, about 1.7 meters, slightly shorter than even Yan Zhusheng.

He had two small, squinty eyes, his beard was cleanly shaven, and he looked a bit simple and naive, with a completely harmless appearance.

It was truly difficult to associate this appearance with the future chief editor.

"Hello, editor." Li Luo reached out to shake Qian Zhou's hand. "I'm Chong Ran."

"I'm Qian Zhou, hello, hello." It was also the first time in Qian Zhou's life meeting one of his authors, and he felt even more nervous than Li Luo.

Especially since this wasn't just a simple meetup with an author; they were also going to meet a star singer like Yuan Wanqing, who was currently a hot topic.

With this in mind, Qian Zhou grew even more nervous. He subconsciously rubbed his hands together and asked Li Luo, "So, are we going directly to the city center now, or should we find a place to eat first?"

"Oh, let's grab a cab first." Li Luo went to the roadside and hailed a taxi, then pointed at Yan Zhusheng and said to his editor, "To her house."

"Huh?"

Sitting in the taxi, Qian Zhou was still completely bewildered, wondering why the two of them were going to a young girl's house for their meetup.

But Li Luo just smiled. "You'll know when we get there."

Although Qian Zhou found it strange, he didn't ask any further, not worried that Li Luo would sell him out.

He usually communicated a lot with Li Luo, and after meeting him in person, he once again confirmed that this sixteen-year-old high school student, though young, had a very mature personality and was very organized.

Recalling what he was like at sixteen, Qian Zhou couldn't help but feel a little ashamed. There was simply no comparison.

So Qian Zhou didn't have any adult arrogance. He chatted casually with Li Luo in the taxi, sharing some industry news and gossip with him.

For instance, a certain author had sold their film and television rights and bought a villa somewhere.

Or which famous authors had been invited to Wenyue Group's upcoming year-end party, all of them big names on the charts.

Speaking of this, Qian Zhou sounded a bit regretful. "If you had published your book a few months earlier, you might have had a chance to go to the party this year."

"When is the party usually held?" Li Luo asked curiously.

In his past life, he was never qualified to attend the party.

Xu Youyu, on the other hand, after becoming one of the Twelve Heavenly Kings and then being promoted to a Great God, was invited to attend every year from then on.

But by then, Li Luo's short drama business had failed, and he owed Xu Youyu a mountain of debt, so he didn't have the face to see her and didn't know the details.

"The time for the party isn't fixed. This year it's around New Year's Day, it's about to be held," Qian Zhou said. "The invitations were sent out in October. You had just hit boutique-level sales back then, so you weren't invited. If you can keep up your current momentum, you'll definitely make it next year."

In this era, for an online author to attend Wenyue Group's year-end party, they basically needed at least ten thousand subscriptions as a baseline.

Or, if their main site sales were at the boutique level, their channel sales had to be explosive.

In short, their commercial value had to meet the standard to be invited to the party, which was considered a recognition of an author's money-making ability.

Li Luo was quite interested, but he didn't feel it was a pity that he couldn't go.

While Li Luo and Qian Zhou were chatting, Yan Zhusheng sat obediently beside Li Luo without saying a word, curiously listening to their conversation.

The taxi stopped at the entrance of Yan Zhusheng's residential complex. After the three of them got out, they walked all the way to Yan Zhusheng's front door.

"So why did we come..." Qian Zhou watched as Yan Zhusheng opened the door, finally unable to resist asking again.

But before he could finish, the door opened, and Yuan Wanqing, who heard the noise from inside, got up from the sofa and came to the door to greet them.

"You're here." Yuan Wanqing looked at Yan Zhusheng and Li Luo, then her gaze fell on Qian Zhou as she asked with confusion, "And this is?"

"This is Li Luo's editor," Yan Zhusheng introduced seriously. "He's here to accompany Li Luo for the interview."

"Oh, I see." Yuan Wanqing smiled gently and took an extra pair of clean slippers from the shoe cabinet. "Come on in, welcome."

At this moment, Qian Zhou was frozen at the doorway, his mouth slightly agape, unable to recover for a long time.

It wasn't until Li Luo waved a hand in front of his face that he snapped out of it, subconsciously opening his mouth and stammering, "Yuan, Yuan, Yuan..."

"That's my classmate's mother," Li Luo said, patting Qian Zhou's shoulder and making the introduction himself. "Let's eat together, and then we'll all go to the city center for the interview in a bit."

(End of this chapter)
